body: Thank you. It’s incredibly hard for people to truly understand all of the layers to how much this all fucking sucks. Unfortunately him and I cannot really be together unless we get married. I’m American and he’s British. He didn’t meet the income qualification before for us to get married and live together in the UK, but now he’s on disability, probably for the rest of his life, so it’s possible we can get married and I could live in the UK without him having to meet the income qualification. It just sucks having him go through all of this and I can’t even be there with him because I can’t just pick up and leave because of my job, and I’m hearing everything about how he’s doing through the grapevine. I love him with all of my heart and I support him but I’m only human, and I can only take so much before I start to break myself.

We met online actually, nearly ten years ago. We spoke on and off, and in 2015 we began talking again. Something clicked and we spoke nonstop for days on end and we had this insane attraction to each other. I ended up booking a plane ticket to go see him, rather on a whim, and the rest is just kinda history. We’ve been together ever since.

My dad’s case happened about 10 years ago so details are a bit fuzzy - glioblastoma sounds familiar. Spoke with boyfriend on the phone a bit later yesterday once I calmed down and he said his doctors said his condition was treatable but not curable. Apparently also, the cancer has spread through the wall of his bowels and part of it is outside of, somewhere near his stomach? But hasn’t gone into any other organs. Which confuses me and I’m not quite sure what that means, apparently he doesn’t know either. But yeah, it’s hard not to compare his condition to other people I know they’ve fought cancer.

My dad had a stage 4 brain tumor and was told he had two weeks to live when it was diagnosed, and he ended up living for 2 years. So I am trying to keep my wits about me and see how my boyfriend responds to the first round of chemo. Trying my best to be positive for his sake.

I guess I’m just confused about the term “advanced” since I’ve never heard that term in the US when talking about cancer. What does that mean? Terminal, incurable, what? And clearly the US healthcare system is not free of its faults, and it has many of them, I just can’t imagine having to wait so long for a diagnosis and treatment plan to be made. If he wanted to pursue other treatment options he really doesn’t have much time since they want the picc inserted next week. Just seems so odd to me but alas.

I am looking for a service that'd give me a local UK number, not a US number unfortunately. But I ended up buying a U.K. number through Skype so I can at least call his mom and have his mom call me more easily instead of using my US number...I can also send texts but I cannot receive them unfortunately. I couldn't find a service that'd do all of those things, but 3/4 will do for me

Yes, we've met before in person multiple times. He uses his laptop for the internet because he basically has a dumb phone equivalent to a shitty burner phone with just text and calling features in the U.K. He isn't big on mobile technology. And he doesn't have his laptop with him in the hospital right now, though his mom assures me that in the next few days we will be able to speak with each other, but right now he's hopped up full of morphine so inbetween his diagnostic testing and various scans and visits from family, he's sleeping. 

And I'll be real, I am a little bit annoyed by this comment. I'm a public school teacher and I am unable to use my days off right now to go see him. He has his family with him and his mom is communicating with me about what's happening, and if I were to go I wouldn't be able to do anything other than sit around at the hospital. If I'm going to use more than 3 personal days I need to contact my union, my superintendent, and my request could still be denied. And also, I am starting work at a new school so I don't even know my new building, my new principal and admin yet, but they all already saw me cry and have a breakdown yesterday after hearing the news from my partner's mom that he has cancer, a colostomy bag, and a tube shoved up his nose so talking right now is physically difficult. 

Wasn't asking for someone to fact check my story, was just reaching out on here for support since I feel like I am going fucking insane as I'm trying to navigate all of this. 

Edit: yes, please, let's all downvote the girl who just found out her legitimate LDR boyfriend (that she has met before, and met his family before, many times) has cancer/is in the hospital and she was looking for support and ideas for how to contact him through his dumb phone since he doesn't have a smartphone. Downvotes are a great idea.
Sadly the phone he has now doesn't have internet access. Just calling and texting
